content.title: Lip-Color Testimonial | Product Raise, Single Application and Camera Return
content.summary: An adult designer demonstrates one lip tint from package proof to a single application result. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One clearly adult host, one room and one product set persist. + Packaging is shown before application. + Only one continuous application gesture occurs. + The applicator returns to its original package. + The final result and product remain visible together.
quick_start.recommended_input: Frame one original adult ceramic designer speaking directly to a vertical handheld camera in one warm studio room. Hold the three-part proof frame for one spoken sentence, keeping label, applicator and face in focus. End with one small head turn showing the finished lip color while the closed tube remains beside the cheek.
required_anchors: One clearly adult host, one room and one product set persist.
The applicator returns to its original package.
The final result and product remain visible together.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: An adult designer demonstrates one lip tint from package proof to a single application result. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.

Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: 固定同一成年人物、卧室镜面和竖屏自拍机位；人物先口播，再让盒装与管装产品同时同框，完成一次唇部涂抹，并以产品在手的妆效近景回到结论。 The reusable mechanism preserves causal order, spatial anchors and the final proof while replacing every source-specific person, location, object, wording, choreography and design.

invariants.rule: One clearly adult host, one room and one product set persist.
invariants.purpose: Establishes the baseline identity, object or geography that every later state must preserve.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact baseline rule, later changes cannot be attributed to the same subject, object or place, so the sequence loses its reference state. Removed rule: "One clearly adult host, one room and one product set persist."

invariants.purpose: Makes the visible trigger precede and explain the first mechanism response.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact trigger rule, the response appears spontaneously and the central cause-and-effect claim is no longer demonstrated. Removed rule: "Packaging is shown before application."

invariants.rule: Only one continuous application gesture occurs.
invariants.purpose: Keeps the middle progression registered instead of allowing an unexplained reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact progression rule, the middle can jump to a replacement state and the accumulated result is no longer traceable. Removed rule: "Only one continuous application gesture occurs."

invariants.rule: The applicator returns to its original package.
invariants.purpose: Reconnects the changed or partial state to the established subject and spatial anchor.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact reconnection rule, detail or transformed shots can belong to a different subject or geography and continuity cannot be verified. Removed rule: "The applicator returns to its original package."

invariants.rule: The final result and product remain visible together.
invariants.purpose: Turns the terminal hold into observable proof that the mechanism completed.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact terminal-proof rule, the sequence stops on motion alone and never confirms the promised outcome or preserved aftermath. Removed rule: "The final result and product remain visible together."
